findings: Residual Go-against-engine divergence outside the 916's classes, reported to the architect, not fixed here and not a regression: a line the browser reads as a block of HTML and goldmark reads as a paragraph of inline HTML keeps its leading 1-3 spaces in the engine and loses them in Go (` </script>`, `  </script>`, `[^f]: a\n\n      <b\t>`), and a lower-case declaration (`<!a>`) is an inline html node to the engine and text to Go. 66 of 12,880 in the html fuzz, 21 of 400 in the indentation fuzz. Measured on the page: a document and a comment of `<!a>` both draw the string `<!a>` (document `<!a>` as text, comment the same string inside `<span data-type="html">`), and ` </script>` draws `</script>` in the document and ` </script>` in the comment. The root cause of the `<!a>` half predates this change and is not block HTML at all: `x <!a> y` reads as text in Go and as an inline html node in the engine at the fork point and at this head alike (goldmark's CommonMark 0.30 declaration rule against micromark's 0.31). At the fork point these same documents drew an empty document or threw `MilkdownError: Cannot create node for doc`, so the change improves every one of them.

The browser engine's html-flow port is faithful: diffing packages/proof-editor/src/html-flow.ts against node_modules/micromark-core-commonmark@2.0.3/dev/lib/html-flow.js leaves exactly one logic change - `return self.interrupt` in place of `return self.interrupt && !self.parser.lazy[self.now().line]` in `tagName` - beside the construct's own name, `blankLine` imported from the package instead of a sibling file, and TypeScript annotations.
